summary: Specifies the Neighbor Discovery protocol for IPv6, which hosts and routers use to find each other, learn link-layer addresses, find routers and detect changes. It replaces ARP for IPv6. It was a draft standard, replaced by RFC 4861.

eli5.summary: On a street, you might shout to find out who lives at a house. This lets computers on a local network find their neighbors and the routers nearby.

questions: how do ipv6 hosts find routers
how does ipv6 neighbor discovery replace arp
what are the neighbor cache states
subtitle: How IPv6 nodes on the same link find each other, find routers, learn link-layer addresses and notice when a neighbor goes away.

tldr.problem: IPv6 nodes on a link need to learn each other's link-layer addresses, find routers and prefixes, and detect when a neighbor or path has failed.
tldr.mechanism: Neighbor Discovery defines five ICMP message types (Router Solicitation and Advertisement, Neighbor Solicitation and Advertisement, and Redirect) plus a reachability-tracking algorithm built on a cache of neighbors.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2461 was a Draft Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 4861, which is the current Neighbor Discovery specification.

today: RFC 2461 was a Draft Standard that obsoleted RFC 1970, and it has itself been obsoleted by RFC 4861. It was also updated by RFC 4311. Use RFC 4861 for the current Neighbor Discovery specification.

sections.title: What Neighbor Discovery Does
sections.content:
The Neighbor Discovery (ND) protocol lets IPv6 nodes, both hosts and routers, determine the link-layer addresses of neighbors on attached links and quickly purge cached values that become invalid. Hosts also use it to find neighboring routers willing to forward packets for them. Nodes use it to keep track of which neighbors are reachable and which are not, and to detect changed link-layer addresses. When a router or the path to it fails, a host actively searches for working alternates.

Unless a document for a particular link type says otherwise, ND applies to all link types. Because it uses link-layer multicast for some services, other mechanisms may be specified on links such as NBMA links. Services that do not depend on multicast, such as redirects, next-hop determination and Neighbor Unreachability Detection, are expected to work as specified here.
sections.eli5: It is the way computers on one local network say hello, find out who is who, and notice when somebody has left.

sections.title: Problems It Solves and How It Differs from IPv4
sections.content:
The RFC lists the problems ND solves: router discovery, prefix discovery, parameter discovery (such as link MTU or hop limit), address autoconfiguration, address resolution, next-hop determination, Neighbor Unreachability Detection, Duplicate Address Detection and redirects. Autoconfiguration itself is specified elsewhere; ND carries the information routers advertise for it, including whether hosts should use stateful (DHCPv6) and/or stateless configuration.

ND corresponds to a combination of the IPv4 protocols ARP, ICMP Router Discovery and ICMP Redirect, with additions. Router Advertisements carry link-layer addresses and prefixes, so no separate netmask mechanism or extra resolution step is needed. Address resolution multicasts are spread over 2^32 multicast addresses, so nodes other than the target are rarely interrupted. Redirects carry the new first hop's link-layer address. Unlike ARP, ND detects half-link failures and avoids sending traffic to neighbors with which two-way connectivity is absent.
sections.eli5: It does the jobs that several different tools did for the older internet, in one package, and it also checks that your neighbor can really hear you back.

sections.title: The Five Messages and Their Options
sections.content:
Router Solicitation (type 133) asks routers to send an advertisement now rather than at their next scheduled time. Router Advertisement (type 134) is sent periodically or in answer; it carries the current hop limit, flags such as M for managed address configuration, a router lifetime, the reachable time and retransmission timer, and options. Neighbor Solicitation (type 135) asks for a neighbor's link-layer address or checks that it is still reachable. Neighbor Advertisement (type 136) answers it, and may also be sent unsolicited to announce a changed link-layer address. Redirect (type 137) tells a host about a better first hop.

Messages can carry options, each with a type and a length in units of 8 octets; a length of 0 is invalid and the packet is discarded. The options defined here are source link-layer address (1), target link-layer address (2), prefix information (3), redirected header (4) and MTU (5). Receivers silently ignore options they do not recognize, which is how the protocol is extended.

All of these messages are sent with a Hop Limit of 255, which matters for security.
sections.eli5: There are five kinds of notes: one asks 'is there a router?', one answers, one asks 'who has this address?', one answers, and one says 'there is a shortcut over here'.

sections.title: Address Resolution and Reachability
sections.content:
To resolve an address, a node multicasts a Neighbor Solicitation to the solicited-node multicast address of the target. The target replies with a unicast Neighbor Advertisement carrying its link-layer address. One request and response is enough for both sides to learn each other's address, because the initiator includes its own in the solicitation. Results are kept in a Neighbor Cache.

Neighbor Unreachability Detection confirms that packets sent to a neighbor reach its IP layer and are processed. Evidence comes from upper-layer hints that a connection is making forward progress, such as new acknowledgments. Without them, the node sends unicast Neighbor Solicitations to the next hop, and only to neighbors it is actively sending packets to.

A Neighbor Cache entry is in one of five states: INCOMPLETE (resolution in progress), REACHABLE (recent confirmation), STALE (no recent confirmation, no action until a packet is sent), DELAY (a packet was sent recently, giving upper layers time to confirm) and PROBE (Neighbor Solicitations are retransmitted until confirmation). Default constants include a REACHABLE_TIME of 30,000 milliseconds and a RETRANS_TIMER of 1,000 milliseconds.
sections.eli5: To find out where a friend sits, you ask the room and only that friend answers. Later, if you have not heard from them in a while, you quietly check they are still there before you keep passing them notes.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
ND can be attacked so that packets flow to unexpected places, enabling denial of service or interception. Without authentication, the protocol limits exposure by ignoring ND packets from off-link senders: every received packet must have a Hop Limit of 255, and since routers decrement the hop limit, such a packet must have come from a neighbor.

A node on the link can still do damage. For example, it can send forged Router Advertisements with a router lifetime of zero for each legitimate router and advertise itself as the default router, sending all traffic through a rogue router. Neighbor Unreachability Detection will not catch this as long as the rogue router answers probes politely. The protocol has no way to decide which neighbors may send Router Advertisements.

The RFC says ND exchanges can be authenticated with the IP Authentication Header, and a node SHOULD include one if a security association exists for the destination. Packets with incorrect authentication MUST be ignored. Administrators SHOULD be able to configure a node to ignore unauthenticated ND messages, although this SHOULD default to allowing them.
sections.eli5: The note only counts if it came from somebody in the same room. Even so, a sneaky person in the room can lie, so there is also a way to sign notes.
